ceo-eng: Quick follow-up to the all-hands runtime segment — leadership asked for a super-brief runbook we can point folks to. Two bullets: exact hosted p95 target, and what triggers an automated rollback during kernel/batching/cache rollouts. Keep it terse. @maya-eng-runtime @leo-eng-sre

maya-eng-runtime: Hosted SLO: p95 token latency <200ms (standard tier). Dedicated: p95 <150ms under committed load. Rollout approach: small traffic canaries -> ramp -> full. Order isn't fixed but recommended: kernel -> batching -> cache.

leo-eng-sre: Rollback triggers (short): auto-rollback if p95 increases >9% OR error-rate absolute increases >0.4% over baseline for a sustained 30m window, or if we observe new OOM/GPU resets. Canary windows: default 24h per step, extend if traffic is bursty.

jamal-ml: Kernel note: some models with short-seq skew may see worse micro-latency after kernel change; we will publish a model-family compatibility table pre-canary. Expect long-context wins, short-context risks.

anya-product: For customers: will Dedicated be able to pin variants? Need a one-line we can use in release notes.

maya-eng-runtime: One-liner: "Dedicated customers can pin a specific model variant per route to prevent automatic runtime updates."

docs-bot: Draft doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/rollout-summary (will add JSON example policy).

ceo-eng: Nice. Action items: maya publish a 2-paragraph FAQ + the JSON policy snippet by EOD; leo add the auto-rollback monitors + pager runbook; product to draft the release note one-liner. Tag me on PRs. :thumbsup:
